briefing.summary: Descend about 800 m to the Lost City Hydrothermal Field, a cluster of towering white carbonate chimneys on the Atlantis Massif. Find and scan the Poseidon tower, then survey the smaller chimneys and the real terrain around the field.
facts: Lost City runs on serpentinization, a chemical reaction between seawater and mantle rock, not on volcanic heat. Its fluid is warm (40-90 degC) and alkaline, unlike a scalding, acidic black smoker.
Poseidon, the tallest tower here, stands about 60 m tall and may be over 100,000 years old.

The published field coordinate is rounded to the nearest arc-minute and, on this tile, lands 1,332 m deep on the massif's south wall -- well outside the field's real 750-900 m range. This mission places the vents on the correct nearby terrain instead; a POI at the original catalog position shows the gap.
The field is only about 500 sq m across, smaller than a single cell of this tile's open bathymetry, so no individual chimney appears in the real terrain.
hazards: Fragile mineral formations: the carbonate spires are delicate and slow-growing. Keep a respectful distance.
Total darkness below a few hundred metres; only your lights work.
